cards.text: This psalm doesn't name its writer, but it opens with a big announcement to the whole world: "The LORD reigns." Three words, friend. THREE WORDS, and the very next line tells the nations how to take it.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD reigns, so the psalm tells the nations to sit back and relax.

cards.text: He's enthroned above the cherubim, and the psalm says, "let the earth quake!" Friend, I used to think the junk drawer getting yanked open was a big shake-up.

cards.question: The psalm says the LORD is great in Zion. How high does it say He is exalted?

cards.text: But shaking isn't the whole response. The psalm calls for praise too, and here comes a short line that's going to keep showing up.

cards.question: The psalm calls for praise to the LORD's great and awesome name. What short reason comes right after?
The psalm calls the LORD the mighty King, and it says this King loves ___.

cards.text: Loving justice is one thing, but this King DID it: "You have established equity; You have exercised justice and righteousness in Jacob." That's Jacob's family, the people of Israel (Gen 32:28).
Then the call goes out: "Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at His footstool; He is holy!" There's that line again.

cards.question: Now the psalm reaches back into Israel's history. Which two brothers does it name among the LORD's priests?

cards.text: That's Moses, Israel's leader, and his brother Aaron (Exod 4:14). Then one more name: Samuel, the prophet who anointed Saul and David (1 Sam 10:1; 16:13), among those who called on His name.

cards.question: True or false: When Moses, Aaron and Samuel called to the LORD, the psalm says He answered.

cards.text: And how did He speak to them? From the pillar of cloud. Me, I jump when my phone buzzes. They got a whole PILLAR OF CLOUD.

cards.question: The LORD spoke from the pillar of cloud and gave them decrees and statutes, and they ___ them.
The psalm talks right to God about these same men. How does it describe Him toward them?

answers.text: Forgiving yet an avenger of their misdeeds
Forgiving so He overlooked their misdeeds
Strict so He never forgave their misdeeds

cards.question: True or false: Because God was forgiving to them, the psalm says their misdeeds didn't matter to Him.

cards.text: One last call to exalt the LORD our God. Earlier it was worship at His footstool, but this time the place is different.

cards.question: Earlier the psalm said the LORD is great in Zion. Now it calls people to worship at His holy ___.

cards.text: And the very last words: "for the LORD our God is holy." That's three times this psalm says He's holy, friend, and once is a line, but three times is the WHOLE POINT.
